title: Harry Kane out of Bayern Munich’s game at Freiburg, Alphonso Davies set for return
content:
Harry Kane is out of Bayern Munich’s game against Freiburg this weekend, but Vincent Kompany has said Alphonso Davies is set to return to action.

Speaking on Friday, Kompany said he was confident Kane, 32, would return against Real Madrid for the Champions League quarter-final first leg on Tuesday but ruled him out of contention for this weekend.

Kane suffered a minor ankle injury while on international duty with England and missed the friendly against Japan on Tuesday.

“Harry trained well until Sunday, then he felt his ankle with the national team,” Kompany said. That affects tomorrow’s game — he won’t be available.

“Still, I’m positive about Tuesday. It’s not ideal, I would have liked to have him against Freiburg, but as of today, that’s not possible.”

Kane is Bayern’s top scorer this season, with 31 goals from 26 Bundesliga appearances, with a further 10 goals in nine Champions League games.

In better news, Kompany confirmed that Canada international Davies and Jamal Musiala are both nearing a return and are available this weekend.

Davies suffered a hamstring strain against Atalanta in the last round of the Champions League and was unable to take part in Canada’s recent internationals against Tunisia and Iceland, while Musiala has missed Bayern’s last three games — and Germany’s recent friendlies against Switzerland and Ghana — having discomfort in his ankle.

Kompany has suggested both will play some part against Freiburg.

“Both are options for the next few games,” Kompany said. “But whether they can play three games in a week or a full 90 minutes is another question.

“But we no longer have the luxury of that much choice. We have to win. And everyone has to deliver to the max and show their best level. We’ll get their quality in the minutes they do play. We try to make logical decisions.”

Bayern have also confirmed that Aleksandar Pavlovic has returned to full training, having had to withdraw from the recent Germany squad, and that goalkeepers Manuel Neuer and Jonas Urbig — who have been carrying thigh and knee injuries respectively — are also in the matchday squad this weekend.
